citations.narrative:
The enclosures for the birds are above the ground attached to metal framework. The metal framework along the bottom of
about 11 of the enclosures is rusted and has broken. There are about twenty two birds throughout the affected
enclosures. Rusted broken frame work may fail to support the enclosures appropriately leading to potential injury to the
enclosed birds.
Housing facilities for birds must be designed and constructed so that they are structurally sound for the species of bird
housed in them. They must be kept in good repair, protect the birds from injury, and restrict other animals from entering
that may negatively affect the welfare of the birds within. The facility must repair, replace or alter the framework in a
manner that ensures the enclosures are safe for the birds.
To be corrected by January 20, 2027.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
Additional Inspectors:
